proposal_origin: Root proposed the stronger character-intersection consequence of the previously retained957triple lemma. This review checks that deduction only; no claim of an independent native discovery or blinded result.

supplied_inputs.prior_grammar_premise: Under the unchanged957role/word-identity contract, an identical whole-word triple requires the SAME form. For the present argument it is enough that at least one occurrence of each cited whole triple form must actually contain the SAME exponent.
supplied_inputs.provenance_limit: These are supplied already-owned strict GDT857triple witnesses, not newly queried or image-adjudicated observations in this review. Their whole-group and working-unit assumptions are retained.

physical_contract: Every SAME realization writes every working unit of one fixed nonempty exponent E inside that complete written word.
The location, contiguity and internal order of those written units may vary. The only necessary condition used is alphabet(E) being a subset of alphabet(word).
No null realization, deletion, distinct allomorph or contextual replacement is licensed by this particular claim. A global bijection may rename the working alphabet consistently.
proof: The first witness has working-unit set {ch,o,l}. The second has {y,t,a,i,n}. Their intersection is empty.
Any fixed E realized fully in both words must satisfy alphabet(E) subset {ch,o,l} intersect {y,t,a,i,n}.
A nonempty finite E has at least one working unit. It cannot have its alphabet contained in the empty set. Contradiction.
For a global bijection pi, pi(A) intersect pi(B)=pi(A intersect B). The empty intersection is invariant; consistent glyph renaming cannot restore a shared nonempty exponent.
strength_and_limits: This strengthens an ending-only argument: prefix, suffix, infix, movable placement and distributed realization of the same nonempty written units all satisfy the subset condition and therefore fail this pair.

It is not necessary to assert that every occurrence of either word has the SAME interpretation. The inherited grammar must, however, require at least one fully written SAME realization in each of the two whole forms. If that premise fails or equal forms can denote different grammatical forms through licensed homography, this deduction alone does not establish the grammar premise.

Several alternative exponents with disjoint alphabets, a zero exponent, elision, or fusion that does not literally retain a common working unit are different physical contracts and are not excluded here.

Different native atomization, nonliteral graphical features or an unbound word boundary also lie outside the supplied working-unit/whole-group comparison. No claim is made that the working units are established native atoms.

No blanket prohibition of morphology, SAME semantics, medial dependency, or the abstract incomplete957module follows. No new carrier, exception, test, source lookup, native count or root-file change was made.
